title: Hiding in Plain Sight: Two New Stick Insects Found in Australian Gardens and Rainforests
title_zh: 藏在眼前：澳大利亚的花园与雨林里发现两种大型竹节虫新种
intro_zh: 本文约 517 词，难度适合 CET-4 水平。文章介绍研究人员在澳大利亚的花园与雨林环境中发现了两种大型竹节虫新种，其中一种的卵带有独特的“盖子”，另有一种过去被合并的竹节虫被重新确认为独立物种。

paragraphs.en: Australia is famous for its wildlife, but even its best-known areas can still hold surprises. Scientists working on a group of large stick insects have discovered two kinds that were not known before. Some of these insects were not hiding in a faraway desert; they were living close to people, in ordinary gardens and in rainforest places that have been studied for many years.
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚以野生动物闻名，但即便是它最知名的地区，也仍然可能藏着意外。研究一类大型竹节虫的科学家发现了两种此前不为人知的竹节虫。其中一些虫子并不是藏在遥远的沙漠里，而是生活在离人很近的地方——普通的花园，以及已被研究多年的雨林地带。

paragraphs.en: Stick insects are experts at looking like plants. Their long, thin bodies copy the shape of twigs, and their brown or green colours blend into the leaves and branches around them. Most of them feed on leaves and move mainly at night, which makes them hard to spot. As a result, a new species may live quietly in a place for years before anyone notices it.
paragraphs.zh: 竹节虫是“伪装成植物”的高手。它们细长的身体模仿树枝的形状，棕色或绿色的体色溶入周围的枝叶之中。它们大多以叶子为食，主要在夜间活动，因此很难被发现。正因如此，一个新物种可能在一个地方安静地生活多年，才终于被人注意到。

paragraphs.en: To sort out these insects, researchers at the University of Sydney revised the Australian members of a group called Anchiale. This group had not been studied closely for a long time, and the old records were mixed together. The team compared body shapes, colours and other physical features, and worked to identify which insects truly belong together.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理清这些昆虫，悉尼大学的研究人员重新审查了一个名为 Anchiale 的类群在澳大利亚的成员。这个类群长期没有得到细致研究，旧有的记录互相混在一起。团队比较了体型、颜色和其他身体特征，努力确定哪些昆虫确实属于同一类。

paragraphs.en: The careful comparison produced two new species. Both are large stick insects, matching the size and build of others in the group. Naming a new species means describing it in detail, so the researchers wrote down clear features that separate these insects from their closest relatives.
paragraphs.zh: 细致的比较带来了两个新物种。它们都是大型竹节虫，体型和结构与该类群中的其他成员相当。为一个新物种命名意味着要详细描述它，因此研究人员写下了能把这两种昆虫与最近亲区分开来的明确特征。

paragraphs.en: One of the two new species has eggs with a unique shape. Each egg carries a small lid, or cap, on top. When the young insect is ready to come out, it pushes this lid open instead of breaking through the whole shell. This lidded egg is different from the eggs of other members of the group, and it gave the scientists a strong clue.
paragraphs.zh: 两个新物种中，有一个的卵形状独特。每枚卵的顶部都带有一个小小的盖状结构。当幼虫准备孵化时，它会把这个盖子顶开，而不必撑破整枚卵壳。这种“带盖”的卵与该类群其他成员的卵不同，为科学家提供了重要线索。

paragraphs.en: The two new species are large, but size alone does not make an insect easy to find. Stick insects sit still for hours, and their bodies look so much like twigs that a person can pass within a metre without noticing anything. Researchers often need to search at night, when the insects are active, and to look carefully at branch after branch.
paragraphs.zh: 这两个新物种体型不小，但仅仅是大并不代表容易找到。竹节虫可以一动不动地待上几个小时，身体看起来太像树枝，以至于人从一米之内走过也可能毫无察觉。研究人员常常需要在夜间——也就是昆虫活跃的时候——逐枝逐枝地仔细寻找。

paragraphs.en: The team also brought back a third species. This insect had been described in the past, then later treated as the same as another kind. After checking the evidence again, the researchers concluded that it deserves its own place on the list, so it was reinstated.
paragraphs.zh: 团队还恢复了第三个物种。这种昆虫过去曾被描述过，后来却被当作与另一种相同。在重新核对证据之后，研究人员认为它应当在名录中拥有自己的位置，于是它被重新确认。

paragraphs.en: What makes the finding interesting is where the insects came from. Some were found in backyards, and others in rainforest areas that many scientists have already visited. These are not empty, unknown landscapes. They are places that people walk through, garden in and study. Yet a large stick insect species can still go unnoticed there for a long time.
paragraphs.zh: 这一发现的有趣之处在于这些昆虫来自哪里。有些是在后院里找到的，另一些则在许多科学家已经造访过的雨林地带。这些并不是空白的、无人知晓的地带，而是人们会走过、会种花种菜、会做研究的地方。然而一个大型竹节虫物种仍能在那里长期不被注意。

paragraphs.en: The work shows that discovery does not always require a trip to a distant place. Looking again at familiar ground, with patience and careful methods, can still uncover something new. For the many small creatures that share our gardens and forests, being watched closely may be the first step towards being understood.
paragraphs.zh: 这项工作表明，发现并不总是需要远行。带着耐心和细致的方法重新审视熟悉的地方，仍可能揭示出新东西。对于与我们共享花园和森林的众多小生物来说，被仔细观察，也许就是它们被了解的第一步。

questions.q: What did the researchers at the University of Sydney do with the group Anchiale?
options: They moved all of its members to a rainforest far away.
They revised its Australian members and recognised two new species.
They proved that all of its members are actually one species.
They collected eggs from gardens across the whole country.
questions.explain: 细节题。文章第三、四段指出，悉尼大学的研究人员重新审查了 Anchiale 类群在澳大利亚的成员，比较身体特征，最后确认了两个新物种。选项 A、C、D 均与原文不符。

questions.q: What is unusual about the eggs of one of the new species?
options: They are laid deep under water.
They change colour with the seasons.
They have a small lid that the young insect pushes open.
They are the largest insect eggs ever recorded.
questions.explain: 细节题。第五段明确说，这个新物种的卵顶部带有一个小小的盖状结构，幼虫孵化时会把它顶开，而不必撑破整枚卵壳。其余选项文中均未提及。

questions.q: Why is the discovery considered surprising?
options: The insects were found in places that scientists have already studied a lot.
The insects are far too small for people to see at all.
The insects live only in deserts far from any city.
The insects had already been named by local gardeners.
questions.explain: 推断题。第八段指出，这些昆虫来自后院和科学家早已造访过的雨林地带，并非空白未知的区域，却长期未被注意到，这正是发现令人意外之处。

questions.q: The word 'reinstated' in the seventh paragraph is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: 词义题。第七段说，这种昆虫过去被描述过，后来被当作与另一种相同，核对证据后研究人员认为它应拥有自己的位置，于是它被“reinstated”，即恢复原有的地位，故与 given back its former position 意思最接近。
